title: Answer
description: The monomorphic wire envelope for a boundary answer whose absence has two provenances (concern class C4, honest absence). Rust is generic (`seam_contracts::Answer<T>`); the wire is NOT — a per-view envelope narrows `value` to that view's payload and inherits the `state`/`reason` discrimination from here, because the repo has no ts-rs generics and a flat generated directory is the wrong place for its first. Emission follows the proven DiversityHint tag/content shape: an adjacent tag (`state`) beside a payload key (`value`) that is simply absent for the non-present states. Authored as a three-branch `oneOf` rather than one object plus conditionals so the generated TypeScript is a genuine discriminated union — a client that checks `state` gets `value` or `reason` narrowed for free, which is the whole point of making C4 survive the boundary. Source of truth for the Rust side: seam_contracts::Answer / AnswerState / AnswerReason (crates/seam-contracts/src/answer.rs).

oneOf.title: AnswerPresent
oneOf.description: The answer arrived and carries a value. Takes no `reason`: 'why is it there' is not a question a boundary answers.

value.description: The payload. A per-view envelope narrows this to that view's type; the base envelope leaves it unconstrained on purpose so one schema can govern every adopting view.

oneOf.title: AnswerAbsent
oneOf.description: The answer arrived and reports the value does not exist. A POSITIVE claim — absence was observed — so its only legal reason is `observed_absent`, and it never carries a value.

oneOf.title: AnswerUnreachable
oneOf.description: No answer arrived; nothing is established in either direction. Always carries a reason — a non-present answer with no reason is exactly the unreadable gauge C8 forbids — and never a value.

_vocabulary.$comment: The two enum schemas this envelope's `state` and `reason` are drawn from. Referenced here rather than by $ref inside the branches because each branch pins a single const/subset — the enums remain the single source of truth for the full vocabulary, and elohim-storage's schema_contract test asserts the branches stay a partition of them.

_adoptions.$comment: Existing three-way surfaces whose states map onto this vocabulary WITHOUT changing their behaviour — the proof that the envelope is adequate rather than aspirational (plan task P1.4). Each mapping is total over the source states it names; elohim/elohim-storage/tests/schema_contract.rs asserts every target below is a legal answer-state. These are read-models of code that already exists; adopting the envelope on the wire is a separate, later change.

epr-pull-status.note: Documents its own 'tri-state' nullable: `total: null` = the desired set cannot be computed yet, which is NOT zero-desired. Rule 11's type specimen.

render-fetch-outcome.note: Already three-way: Arrived{empty} splits truthful-empty from Stalled, and RenderTerminal keeps the same seam. `arrived_empty` is an OBSERVED emptiness — the fetch settled — so it is `absent`, not `unreachable`.

doorway-reconcile-decision.note: The third independent derivation of honest absence; `ReconcileDecision::answer_state()` is the live projection of this mapping in Rust. UpToDate and Stale are both PRESENT answers — which head they name is a verdict on top of the answer, not a different kind of answer.

storage-local-resolve.note: The first adoption. `Probe` is deliberately outside the triad — 'I have not asked' is an instruction, not an answer.
